chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, he raised it (to the Prophet) and said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) heard a man saying, 'I am free from the religion of Muhammad.' The Messenger of Allah said to him, 'Woe to you! If you are free from the religion of Muhammad, then upon whose religion will you be?' He said, and the Messenger of Allah did not speak to him until he died.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person who declares they are free from the religion of Muhammad?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet’s inquiry, 'Upon whose religion will you be?', highlights the theological necessity of a positive affiliation rather than mere negation of Islam, a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding apostasy. The man’s subsequent silence is interpreted by scholars as a tacit admission of his departure from the faith, sealing his status as a *murtadd* (apostate). This incident underscores the gravity of verbal renunciation in Islamic law, where the absence of a counter-claim to another valid religion often suffices for judgment.
